speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. To help me understand your condition better, have you noticed any specific changes in your stool or urine recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hepatitis A.

Based on your history of attending a state fair with potentially contaminated food, combined with dark urine, fatigue, fever, and abdominal pain, these are classic signs of viral hepatitis. I will order blood tests to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, Hepatitis_A_IgM_Antibody.
